trials.hypothesis: The target channels get their own stem and a learned 64x64 mixing over all cells (with a residual), so the network can learn the 4-column roll. The build stream stays local. The merged features feed the original conv trunk and pooled brick heads. ent_coef is raised to 0.02 to slow the collapse to DONE. Refuted if dev success stays near 0 and the agent still presses DONE straight away (episode length about 1).

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"ent_coef": 0.02}

BST = 32
TST = 64
TC = 32
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        Z = int(spec.Z)
        self.Z = Z
        self.Y = int(spec.Y)
        self.X = int(spec.X)
        n = self.Y * self.X
        self.bstem = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(Z + 2, BST, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.tstem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3 * Z + 1, TST, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(TST, TC, 1))
        self.tmix = nn.Linear(n, n)
        self.merge = nn.Conv2d(BST + TC, COL, 1)
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        Z = self.Z
        B = obs.shape[0]
        bld = torch.cat([obs[:, :Z], obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 1], obs[:, 4 * Z + 2:4 * Z + 3]], dim=1)
        tgt = torch.cat([obs[:, Z:4 * Z], obs[:, 4 * Z + 1:4 * Z + 2]], dim=1)
        b = self.bstem(bld)
        t = self.tstem(tgt)
        tm = self.tmix(t.flatten(2)).reshape(B, -1, self.Y, self.X)
        t = F.relu(t + tm)
        s = F.relu(self.merge(torch.cat([b, t], dim=1)))
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.name: factorised axis-mix both streams
trials.hypothesis: This replaces the full 64x64 cell mixing with small learned XxX and YxY mixes along rows and columns, each with a residual. import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"ent_coef": 0.02}

BST = 32
TST = 64
TC = 32
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class AxisMix(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, Y, X):
        super().__init__()
        self.mx = nn.Linear(X, X)
        self.my = nn.Linear(Y, Y)

    def forward(self, t):
        a = self.mx(t)
        b = self.my(t.transpose(2, 3)).transpose(2, 3)
        return t + a + b


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        Z = int(spec.Z)
        self.Z = Z
        Y = int(spec.Y)
        X = int(spec.X)
        self.bstem = nn.Conv2d(Z + 2, BST, 1)
        self.bmix = AxisMix(Y, X)
        self.tstem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3 * Z + 1, TST, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(TST, TC, 1))
        self.tmix = AxisMix(Y, X)
        self.merge = nn.Conv2d(BST + TC, COL, 1)

        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)

import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"ent_coef": 0.02}

BST = 32
TW = 48
TC = 32
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)

    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        Z = int(spec.Z)
        X = int(spec.X)
        self.Z = Z
        self.pl = X // 2
        self.pr = X - 1 - X // 2
        self.bstem = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(Z + 2, BST, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.trow = nn.Conv2d(3 * Z + 1, TW, (1, X))
        self.tproj = nn.Conv2d(TW, TC, 1)
        self.merge = nn.Conv2d(BST + TC, COL, 1)
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        Z = self.Z
        bld = torch.cat([obs[:, :Z], obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 1], obs[:, 4 * Z + 2:4 * Z + 3]], dim=1)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"ent_coef": 0.05}

BST = 32
TW = 48
TC = 32
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        Z = int(spec.Z)
        X = int(spec.X)
        self.Z = Z
        self.pl = X // 2
        self.pr = X - 1 - X // 2
        self.bstem = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(Z + 2, BST, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.trow = nn.Conv2d(3 * Z + 1, TW, (1, X))
        self.tproj = nn.Conv2d(TW, TC, 1)
        self.merge = nn.Conv2d(BST + TC, COL, 1)
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        Z = self.Z
        bld = torch.cat([obs[:, :Z], obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 1], obs[:, 4 * Z + 2:4 * Z + 3]], dim=1)
        tgt = torch.cat([obs[:, Z:4 * Z], obs[:, 4 * Z + 1:4 * Z + 2]], dim=1)
        b = self.bstem(bld)
        tp = F.pad(tgt, (self.pl, self.pr, 0, 0), mode='circular')
        t = F.relu(self.tproj(F.relu(self.trow(tp))))
        s = F.relu(self.merge(torch.cat([b, t], dim=1)))
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"ent_coef": 0.02}

BST = 32
TW = 48
TC = 32
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32
MC = 32


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        Z = int(spec.Z)
        X = int(spec.X)
        self.Z = Z
        self.pl = X // 2
        self.pr = X - 1 - X // 2
        self.bstem = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(Z + 2, BST, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.trow = nn.Conv2d(3 * Z + 1, TW, (1, X))
        self.tproj = nn.Conv2d(TW, TC, 1)
        self.merge = nn.Conv2d(BST + TC, COL, 1)
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.mstem = nn.Conv2d(2 * Z + 1, MC, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH + 2 * MC, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        Z = self.Z
        bld = torch.cat([obs[:, :Z], obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 1], obs[:, 4 * Z + 2:4 * Z + 3]], dim=1)
        tgt = torch.cat([obs[:, Z:4 * Z], obs[:, 4 * Z + 1:4 * Z + 2]], dim=1)
        mis = torch.cat([obs[:, 2 * Z:4 * Z], obs[:, 4 * Z + 2:4 * Z + 3]], dim=1)
        b = self.bstem(bld)
        tp = F.pad(tgt, (self.pl, self.pr, 0, 0), mode='circular')
        t = F.relu(self.tproj(F.relu(self.trow(tp))))
        s = F.relu(self.merge(torch.cat([b, t], dim=1)))
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        place = self.head(f)
        m = F.relu(self.mstem(mis))
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3)), m.mean((2, 3)), m.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"ent_coef": 0.02, "ppo_epochs": 2}

BST = 32
TW = 48
TC = 32
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32
MC = 32


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        Z = int(spec.Z)
        X = int(spec.X)
        self.Z = Z
        self.pl = X // 2
        self.pr = X - 1 - X // 2
        self.bstem = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(Z + 2, BST, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.trow = nn.Conv2d(3 * Z + 1, TW, (1, X))
        self.tproj = nn.Conv2d(TW, TC, 1)
        self.merge = nn.Conv2d(BST + TC, COL, 1)
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.mstem = nn.Conv2d(2 * Z + 1, MC, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH + 2 * MC, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        Z = self.Z
        bld = torch.cat([obs[:, :Z], obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 1], obs[:, 4 * Z + 2:4 * Z + 3]], dim=1)

TW = 48
TC = 32
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40

analyses.1: There are no trials yet. The starting network collapsed to DONE on the first step (episode length 1.0 by 25% of training). I think the hidden rule causes this. Target, missing and extra channels are rolled 4 columns, so the useful target information for an anchor at column x sits at x+4. That is outside the receptive field of two 3x3 convolutions. Every placement therefore looks like it has negative expected reward, and DONE (reward 0) wins. The first fix is to give the network a learned global spatial mixing of the target channels, so it can learn the realignment, while keeping the build stream local. Round 1 tests three things: a full token-mixing realigner, the same network with a recipe giving more updates and samples, and a cheaper factorised row/column mixer applied to both streams. All three raise entropy slightly to slow the collapse to DONE. A 2-seed mean above 0 would already beat the 0.000 baseline.
analyses.2: All four trials so far, the starting network included, score 0. Each one collapses to DONE within 25 to 50% of training. Here is why. The target channels are rolled X/2 = 4 columns, so a 3x3 trunk sees a missing cell 4 columns away from where the brick has to go. Placements therefore look random and lose reward on average, while DONE pays 0. Once the policy settles on DONE, a good single placement would still score above zero, so it could learn from there, but only if the network can line the target up with the build. Round 1 tried to do that with layers that are not translation-equivariant: a full 64x64 cell mix, and an axis mix whose single 8x8 matrix is shared across every channel. Neither learned the shift before the collapse. Giving it more updates (r1c2) only made the collapse come sooner. Next I try a learned, translation-equivariant, circular full-width convolution, so that every cell and every placement teaches the same offset. One candidate applies it only to the target channels, one applies it generically to all channels on both axes, and one raises the entropy bonus to slow the collapse.
analyses.3: The circular (1,X) row convolution is what made the task learnable: all non-circular variants stayed at 0 (DONE at once), all circular ones trained (0.447 target-only, 0.325 generic, 0.339 with entropy 0.05). Seeds for one setting differ by 0.11 to 0.16, so differences among the circular variants are probably noise; higher entropy did not help. Two limits on the best run: (1) training success was still climbing at the end (0.21 at 75%, 0.29 at 100%) and runs used about 65 of 900 s, so more samples look worthwhile; (2) the failures are early DONEs. IoU is 0.885 with almost no wrong cells, and the traces stop with missing cells left, often upper layers. The DONE and value heads only see trunk pooling, which the shift blurs. Missing and extra counts do not change under the shift, so a learned per-cell layer followed by global pooling gives a clean stop signal. Test: more samples, the DONE fix, and both together.
analyses.4: Every trial without a circular row convolution on the target channels scored 0: the agent learned to press DONE at once. The circular (1, X) convolution unlocked learning (r2c1: 0.447). The generic axial version (0.325) and ent_coef 0.05 (0.339) were no better, given the seed noise. Halving PPO epochs from 4 to 2 nearly doubled the samples and gave the clearest gain (r3c1: 0.699, training success still rising at 0.675). So the run is short of samples, not of optimisation per sample. The missing/extra pooling for the DONE head did not help (0.404, and 0.297 with 2 epochs, where one seed scored 0.078). Seed spread is large, up to about 0.44 between seeds. In this final round I push the sample-count lever further, to 1 PPO epoch (about 367k steps), and test a higher learning rate and more frequent smaller updates on top of it. The architecture stays fixed at r3c1, the best so far.
